title: How to cut a long video for TikTok on iPhone
description: Prepare a long recording for TikTok on iPhone, review ReelClip’s cut modes, and learn how Apple Intelligence works with sampled video frames.
primaryKeyword: how to cut a long video for tiktok

blocks.html: You have a 12-minute talking-head video, a stream recording, or a long vlog — and you want three or four TikTok-ready clips out of it. You can prepare those clips directly on your iPhone, review each moment, and save the ones you want to post. How long it takes depends on the recording, your device, and how much you edit.

blocks.html: What you need

• The long recording already in your Photos library, or in the Files app.
  • An iPhone running iOS 17 or later, as listed for the current app release.
  • ReelClip (free to import and preview; saving or exporting requires Creator mode). AI features have additional hardware and software requirements, including compatible, enabled Apple Intelligence. Check availability on your device.

attributes.class: text-2xl sm:text-3xl font-black tracking-tight mt-12 mb-4

blocks.html: The 7-step workflow
1. Import the recording into ReelClip
Import your recording from Photos or Files. ReelClip copies it into its private sandbox — the original file in Photos stays untouched, and nothing is uploaded.
2. Pick the right cut mode
There are four cut modes. Pick the one that matches your source material:

• Cut — splits the video into equal-duration pieces. Good when the recording has clear segments (interview sections, list items, chapters).
  • Transcript — runs on-device speech recognition, finds the pauses, and lets you trim the dead air. Good for talking-head content and podcasts.
  • Slice — choose a moment yourself, move the selection and refine its start and end.
  • AI — describe what you want (“the funniest moment”, “the part where I explain the pricing”, “the most quotable line”). Apple Intelligence can help interpret the request and propose moments for you to review when the feature is available on your device.

blocks.html: How Apple Intelligence works in ReelClip 1.5

ReelClip 1.5 adds an on-device request assistant for AI recipes. It opens in a separate sheet and can help clarify a request or separate what should be found in pictures from what should be found in speech. Review the suggestion, edit it, or cancel and keep your original wording. It does not change the clip-count or duration controls, and it does not start a search until you accept.

On an iPhone running iOS 27 with an available Apple Intelligence model and a supported language, ReelClip 1.5 can also use the Foundation Models framework’s image input for visual requests. The app checks sampled still frames and ties a proposed moment to its source time. On iOS 26, visual requests continue to use on-device Vision observations instead. See Apple’s guide to image prompting with Foundation Models.

This is sampled-frame analysis, not continuous viewing of every frame. A brief action between samples can be missed, and a selected moment still needs your review. Visual analysis cannot confirm music, silence, tone of voice, or other sound-only conditions.

Availability checked 25 October 2026: Apple’s public App Store listing is still version 1.4.3. The request assistant and the iOS 27 image-input path are in ReelClip 1.5 TestFlight build 518, so these features are not yet in the public App Store version. Direct image input also requires iOS 27, a supported language, and an available Apple Intelligence model.
3. Review every planned clip

This is the step people skip, and it is the one that matters. Tap each planned clip, watch it from start to finish, and either keep, trim, or reject it. ReelClip never auto-exports. You decide what ships.
4. Trim each clip to TikTok length

Give each clip one complete idea. Tighten the start, remove any unnecessary lead-in, and keep enough context for someone who has never seen the full recording. Check TikTok’s current upload limits before posting; there is no universal ideal clip length.
5. Check the framing for a vertical post

If your source video is landscape, you have two choices: export as is, or crop it for a vertical post in your finishing editor. Choosing a time range and choosing the picture framing are separate decisions; inspect both before posting.
6. Save the batch to Photos

Tap Review and wait for the clips to finish preparing. Play the outputs, then choose the save action for Photos. Wait for the completion confirmation before leaving the app. Saving or exporting a finished video requires Creator mode; the originals stay intact.
7. Upload to TikTok from Photos

Open TikTok, tap the plus button, then Upload. Pick the first clip from your library. TikTok will pull it from your device — ReelClip never had access to your TikTok account and never uploaded anything to TikTok’s servers.

blocks.html: Common pitfalls

• Skipping the review. The AI mode is good but not perfect. Always watch each clip start-to-finish before exporting.
  • Uploading the original 12-minute file. Keep the source, then choose a version that fits the story and destination. A shorter clip does not guarantee more views.
  • No captions. Captions help people follow speech when they cannot listen. Check their spelling and timing in your finishing editor before posting.

blocks.html: What to do after TikTok

Before cross-posting to YouTube Shorts or Instagram Reels, check each platform’s current format and length requirements. The same moment may need different framing or duration for each destination. Read our guide to video length and reach for the platform distinctions, or see how to extract podcast highlights for a related workflow.
